verdict.rationale: Temporal documents a self-hosted guide for running its open source orchestration infrastructure, with Docker, Kubernetes, or manual deployment paths to a production-ready Temporal Service. The GitHub repo and a local `temporal server start-dev` command corroborate that the core server is available to run yourself. A community user also reports running it in OSS projects. Missing for 10: hands-on independent evidence of a production self-hosted deployment (corroboration is mainly the repo and dev-server command).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: This guide shows you how to self-host open source infrastructure software that orchestrates your durable applications.
Choose a deployment approach (Docker, Kubernetes, or manual) and set up a production-ready Temporal Service.
This starts a complete Temporal Service with Web UI on your local machine.
